questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the cost and revenue curves for a pizza in a popular high street restaurant. The restaurant currently pursues an objective of revenue maximisation. Calculate the change in total supernormal profit if the restaurant changes its objective from revenue maximisation to profit maximisation. You are advised to show your working.
Using an example from your own knowledge, explain the distinction between renewable and non-renewable resources.

In 2022 the UK government provided 130 new licences for North Sea oil and gas exploration, in order to reduce energy prices. However, companies can take 20 years to begin to extract oil. Furthermore, they often have to continue producing oil even when prices fall because the equipment has no other uses. With reference to the data above, explain the likely numerical value of the price elasticity of supply for oil.

In 2021, a bakery sold 2.5 million sausage rolls per week at the price of £1.00 each. In 2022 the price increased to £1.20. The price elasticity of demand was estimated to be −0.2. Calculate the new quantity of sausage rolls sold per week in 2022 after the price increased, ceteris paribus.
The economy of Singapore is a highly developed free market economy with some elements of government intervention. Define the term ‘free market’.

The diagram below shows the equilibrium position of a dental practice operating in a monopolistically competitive industry. The government subsidises dental care in the UK through the National Health Service (NHS). There has been a large decrease in the work carried out by NHS dentists. Up to 90% of practices are not accepting new NHS patients. Draw an externalities diagram to identify the welfare gain area from the consumption of dental care in the UK.
Explain why public goods may not be provided by the private sector.

Nearly 750 000 consumers in Britain face unresolved problems with used car purchases every year. Older vehicles tend to have more faults and increase the risks facing a potential buyer. With reference to the data above, explain how imperfect market information may lead to a misallocation of resources in the used-car market.
Explain how the operation of market forces will eliminate an excess supply of coffee.

The National Minimum Wage for people over 23 rose by 9.7% to £10.42 in April 2023. The industry most affected is hospitality. Draw a labour market diagram to show the likely impact of the increase in the National Minimum Wage for hospitality employees.

In March 2019, 458 054 new car registrations were made, which subsequently fell by 44% in March 2020 due to the impact of the global health crisis. Demand for new vehicles can change quickly and can be caused by a variety of factors. The diagram on the previous page shows new car registrations in March from 2007 to 2023. Using 2010 as the base year, calculate the index number for 2023.
With reference to Extract A, explain one likely impact of the growth of digital markets on allocative efficiency.

With reference to Extract B, explain why the change to meat-substitute products may result in an increase in the revenue of food companies. Refer to the concept of price elasticity of demand in your answer.
With reference to Extract C, examine two effects of increased ‘automation’ on the demand for labour.
With reference to the information provided and your own knowledge, assess the view that consumers switching to meat-substitute products is an example of rational behaviour.
With reference to the information provided, discuss whether the price elasticity of demand for video games is elastic or inelastic.
With reference to the last paragraph of Extract B, explain two factors which are likely to influence price elasticity of supply.
With reference to the information provided, assess whether the market for video game development is contestable.
Using examples from either Extract A or Extract B, explain what is meant by positive and normative economic statements.
Discuss the likely benefits of mergers for firms such as Microsoft.
With reference to Extract A, discuss the likely private costs and external costs caused by meat farming. Use an appropriate diagram in your answer.
Evaluate the likely microeconomic effects of a reduction in subsidies to farmers of animal products (Figure 1 and Extract B, line 14). Use a relevant diagram to support your answer.
Evaluate the likely microeconomic effects of an increase in indirect tax on animal products (Figure 2 and Extract A, line 17). Use a relevant diagram to support your answer.

High Speed 2 (HS2) was a £100 billion UK government rail project designed to expand the existing network. The journey time between London and Manchester would take just 1 hour and 11 minutes, 54 minutes quicker than today’s fastest time. Almost 900 homes, 1 000 businesses and around 60 ancient woodlands would be destroyed by its construction. Evaluate the likely microeconomic effects of building major infrastructure projects.

In 2023, the UK prime minister Rishi Sunak said that he wanted to see all students in England study some form of mathematics until they reach the age of 18 to ‘ensure that they leave school better equipped for the jobs of the future’. This would require additional spending on education. Just half of all 16 to 19 year-olds study mathematics. Yet in a world where data is everywhere and statistics are vital in every job, the workforce will require more analytical skills than ever before. Evaluate the likely microeconomic effects of increased spending on education.
Selected economic data on Morocco and Pakistan, 2021, constant values. With reference to the data provided, explain one limitation of using GDP to compare living standards between countries.

Between January 2020 and December 2020, the rate of unemployment in the UK increased from 3.9% to 5.2%. This was as a result of the UK economy experiencing a recession. With reference to the information above, explain one possible effect of the increase in the rate of unemployment on the UK government budget.

UK current account of the balance of payments, percentage of GDP, 2012–2022. With reference to the chart on the previous page, explain one likely reason for the change in the UK current account deficit from 2016 to 2021.

The table shows average UK house prices between January 2023 and March 2023. Explain one likely impact of the fall in average UK house prices on existing homeowners between January 2023 and March 2023. Refer to the table on page 4 in your answer.
UK real GDP percentage growth, quarter 1 (Q1) 2022 to quarter 1 (Q1) 2023. Explain one likely disadvantage of a decline in GDP on: (i) workers (ii) government.
It was forecast that the UK will experience a positive output gap in 2024. Explain one reason why it is difficult to measure the size of an output gap in an economy.
It was forecast that the UK will experience a positive output gap in 2024. Define the term ‘trade cycle’.
China terms of trade index (base year 2000 = 100), 2010–2020. Explain what is meant by ‘terms of trade’.
In 2023 the UK government reduced indirect tax on certain goods and services. Define the term ‘indirect tax’.

In 2023 the UK government reduced indirect tax on certain goods and services. Annotate the aggregate demand (AD) and short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) diagram below to show the likely impact of a reduction in indirect tax on the equilibrium level of real output and the price level.

China terms of trade index (base year 2000 = 100), 2010–2020. Explain the likely impact of the change in China’s terms of trade from 2012 to 2020 on China’s current account. Assume that demand for China’s exports and imports is price elastic.

The UK’s labour force inactivity rate was 20.2% in January 2020 and increased to 21.5% in January 2022. After an increase in the early stages of the global health crisis, most developed countries have recorded a decrease in the inactivity rate back to, and below, levels in 2019. This is not the case in the UK. The total UK labour force in January 2022 was 34.5 million. With reference to the information above, calculate the total number of inactive people in the UK labour force in January 2022.

The UK’s labour force inactivity rate was 20.2% in January 2020 and increased to 21.5% in January 2022. After an increase in the early stages of the global health crisis, most developed countries have recorded a decrease in the inactivity rate back to, and below, levels in 2019. This is not the case in the UK. Explain one likely reason for the high levels of inactivity in the UK labour force.

The UK net monthly balance of trade in goods and services, by value, January 2023 to October 2023, is shown in the chart below. Explain one likely reason for the deficit in the UK balance of trade in goods and services. Refer to the chart on page 10 in your answer.
With reference to Figure 1, explain the distinction between direct and indirect taxation.
With reference to Figure 1, explain the term ‘rate of economic growth’.
With reference to Extract A, examine two factors influencing the short‑run aggregate supply of the German economy.
With reference to the first paragraph of Extract A, explain the likely relationship between real incomes and subjective happiness.
With reference to the information provided and your own knowledge, assess the likely macroeconomic effects of the German government’s budget deficit.
With reference to Extract A and your own knowledge, assess the limitations of using GDP to compare living standards over time.

With reference to Extract B, discuss the impact of the planned investment by Intel in a new semiconductor factory on Germany’s aggregate demand. Use an aggregate demand and aggregate supply diagram in your answer.
With reference to the information provided, explain two factors that the Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee may have considered when changing the base interest rate.
Discuss supply‑side policies the German government could use ‘to improve its economic performance’ (Extract A, line 6).
Discuss the likely macroeconomic effects of a decrease in government expenditure on the UK economy. Use an aggregate demand and aggregate supply diagram to support your answer.
Evaluate the possible causes of inflation in the UK.
Evaluate the use of market-based supply-side policies to increase UK employment.

In January 2023 the UK prime minister, Rishi Sunak, promised to halve inflation by the end of the year. In July 2023 the Bank of England governor, Andrew Bailey, said: “It is crucial that we… return inflation to its 2% target and provide the environment of price stability in which the UK economy can thrive. This is the best contribution monetary policy can make to the prosperity of the United Kingdom.” Evaluate the possible conflicts between macroeconomic objectives when seeking to control inflation.

In Sudan, public services such as healthcare are struggling to keep running. Power outages, blocking of internet access, and fuel shortages, will mean hospitals struggle to operate. Many of the hospitals in the capital city, Khartoum, have reported shortages of doctors, blood, transfusion equipment, medical supplies, and other skilled workers and commodities. Evaluate the possible factors influencing the level of economic development in a developing country of your choice.
Explain one reason why consumers buy less than the social optimum quantity of healthy food.
With reference to Extract B, examine two likely reasons why wages in supermarkets are above the National Minimum Wage of £10.42.
With reference to Figure 1 and Extract C, discuss whether supermarkets charging similar prices for petrol is evidence of collusion. Use game theory to support your answer.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of high levels of inflation. Refer to the UK or any other developed economy in your answer.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of a regional trade agreement between the UK and the EU.
Using a demand and supply diagram, explain the cost of a subsidy on the market for cooking oil to the Indian government (Extract E, line 6).
Examine two advantages of using the Human Development Index (HDI) to measure the level of economic development in India.
With reference to Extract F, discuss the problems that might be involved with the buffer stock system in India.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic reasons for the fall in poverty in India.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of rapid increases in population in India.

The table below shows price elasticity of demand for bus tickets in London 2021 Explain one likely reason for the difference in the price elasticity of demand for the 18+ student bus ticket and the adult bus ticket.

Scarcity of non‑renewable resources, such as oil, is a key reason why alternative resources have been developed by economies. In recent years, within the energy market there has been a large increase in the production of wind power. With reference to the information provided, explain the distinction between renewable and non‑renewable resources.
The table below shows price elasticity of supply for housing in the US in 2020. With reference to the data above, explain one likely reason for the difference in the price elasticity of supply.

Vanilla bean prices increased to a record $600 a kilogramme in 2018 after a cyclone hit the tropical island of Madagascar, damaging crops. Madagascar supplies 75% to 80% of the world vanilla bean market. Define the term ‘supply.’

Vanilla bean prices increased to a record $600 a kilogramme in 2018 after a cyclone hit the tropical island of Madagascar, damaging crops. Madagascar supplies 75% to 80% of the world vanilla bean market. Annotate the diagram below to show the effect of the cyclone on the price of vanilla beans.

Peloton is a firm which makes exercise bikes. Peloton’s objective is to prioritise selling fitness services rather than to achieve short-term profit maximisation. Draw a cost and revenue diagram to illustrate the different business objectives: profit maximisation and revenue maximisation.

Singapore is mainly a free market economy. The education system in Singapore produces some of the highest achieving students in international education rankings, with its teenagers coming top in tests in mathematics, reading and science. Singapore’s education system is provided by the state. With reference to the information above, explain why education is normally provided by the state.

In 2022 the government announced that the maximum undergraduate tuition fee for universities in England will remain at £9 250 per year for the next two years. Explain one likely reason for the maximum price for an undergraduate university programme.

Statement 1 Finland has schools with an average class size of 19.6 Statement 2 Other countries ought to set school class sizes similar to Finland. 5% of total government spending in Finland is on education and therefore other areas of the economy have reduced funding as a result, including the military despite an increase in recent global conflicts. With reference to the information above, explain what is meant by ‘opportunity cost’.

The graph below shows the largest mortgage lenders in the United Kingdom (UK) in 2020, by market share. With reference to the information on the preceding page, explain the market structure of mortgage lending in the UK.

Chief Executive Elon Musk said “affordability” was the biggest barrier to Tesla reaching a far larger market. Before recent price cuts for its electric vehicles, he said, “We weren’t sure about what the price elasticity of demand was for Tesla. We found that even small changes in price have a big impact on demand.” In June 2023, Tesla further reduced the price of its Model 3 vehicle by £4 200 from £42 990. It has been forecast that the price cut will lead to a 15% increase in demand. Ceteris paribus, calculate the price elasticity of demand for the Model 3. You are advised to show your working.

Chief Executive Elon Musk said “affordability” was the biggest barrier to Tesla reaching a far larger market. Before recent price cuts for its electric vehicles, he said, “We weren’t sure about what the price elasticity of demand was for Tesla. We found that even small changes in price have a big impact on demand.” Define the term ‘ceteris paribus’.
With reference to Extract A, explain the likely reasons for the change in price of electronic devices. Include a supply and demand diagram in your answer.
Explain what is meant by the ‘unintended consequence’ (Extract B, line 9) of the plastic tax.
Examine two factors which might influence the supply of labour in the electronics industry.
With reference to Extract A and your own knowledge, assess the view that it is irrational to buy plastic carrier bags when shopping.
Assess whether firms in the electronics industry benefit from economies of scale.
With reference to Extract A, explain the likely numerical value for the income elasticity of demand for reusable cleaning products.
Discuss the likely concerns of the competition authorities regarding the proposed merger of the two companies referred to in Extract C.
With reference to Extract C, explain how incentives to use reusable coffee cups may lead to a fall in demand for single‑use cups.
With reference to Extract D, discuss possible methods of government intervention to reduce electronic waste.
Discuss the likely private costs and external costs of the production of plastic.
Evaluate the likely impact of a tax on plastic food-packaging. Use a diagram to support your answer.
Evaluate methods of government intervention which could be used to reduce the market failure associated with plastic waste. Use a diagram to support your answer.

A small hotel in Scarborough has seen its energy bills increase from £2 000 to £8 000 per month. Small businesses do not have the energy management teams of larger companies to negotiate better deals. Evaluate the microeconomic effects of rising energy bills on the hotel industry or an industry of your choice.

Bytedance, which owns TikTok, has launched its own fragrance ‘Emotif’. The Beijing-based social media giant has already entered the food and drink markets. Evaluate the level of contestability in the fragrance industry or another industry of your choice.

UK household savings as a percentage of household disposable income, quarter 1 (Q1) 2015 to quarter 3 (Q3) 2021 In Q4 of 2015 average household disposable income was £26 300. Calculate the total amount of money saved by the average household in Q4 of 2015.

In 2019 the average annual percentage increase in real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was 1.7% in developed countries and it was 4.6% in developing countries. Explain one limitation of using GDP data to compare living standards between developed and developing countries.

UK household savings as a percentage of household disposable income, quarter 1 (Q1) 2015 to quarter 3 (Q3) 2021 Explain one likely reason for the change in total household savings from Q1 2020 to Q2 2020.
In 2019 the marginal propensity to consume in the UK was estimated to be 0.8. Define the term ‘marginal propensity to consume’.
Investment in the European Union, percentage of GDP, January 2019 to October 2021 With reference to the data, explain one likely effect of the fall in investment in 2020.
In 2019 the marginal propensity to consume in the UK was estimated to be 0.8. Explain one likely factor that could increase the level of consumption of UK households.

A group of banks, including Barclays and JP Morgan, have been fined more than €1 billion by the EU’s competition authorities for rigging the foreign exchange market after the Global Financial Crisis of 2008. The EU found that traders at the banks had used online chat rooms to share information about customers’ orders, prices and other trading activities in order to manipulate the currency markets. With reference to the information above, explain what is meant by ‘market rigging’.

The graph below shows UK long-term migration trends, September 2013 to September 2019. Immigration refers to the number of people entering the country to live there and emigration refers to the number of people leaving the country. With reference to the above chart, explain one likely effect of migration on employment in the UK.
Business investment fell by 0.5% between Quarter 3 2019 and Quarter 4 2019. Define the term ‘investment’.
In July 2020 a survey estimated that the marginal propensity to consume in the UK was 0.1. Calculate the total increase in aggregate demand from an increase in government spending of £60 million.

Business investment fell by 0.5% between Quarter 3 2019 and Quarter 4 2019. Annotate the aggregate demand (AD) and short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) diagram below to show the likely impact of a fall in business investment on the equilibrium level of real output and the price level.
In March 2018 the US imposed a tariff of 25% on steel imports from the UK. Explain the likely impact of this tariff on the steel market in the US.
The table below shows the UK’s budget deficit between March 2016 and March 2019. Define the term ‘budget deficit’.

The table below shows the UK’s budget deficit between March 2016 and March 2019. Using the above table, calculate the percentage decrease in budget deficit between March 2016 and March 2019. You are advised to show your working.
With reference to Figure 4 and your own knowledge, explain the distinction between a progressive and a regressive tax.
With reference to Figure 1, explain the term ‘inflation rate’.
